content:
incident-bot: PAGE FIRED — PagerDuty incident INC-4321: service=inference-runtime, metric=p99_latency_eu-west, value=2.9s (>2.5s), window=3m. Severity: P1. Link: https://pagerduty.example/INC-4321
PagerDuty: Alert routed to rotation: @Jordan (on-call). Escalation policy: after 4m -> @Sam.
Jordan: acked the pager :white_check_mark:
Jordan: I'm looking at the dashboard now — p99 spike started ~05:12 UTC, coincides with a KV eviction spike on sidecar pool-eu-west.
Priya: seeing repeated kv_evict spikes and sidecar OOM-ish logs, maybe backpressure from a noisy model batch. Logs:
```
[05:11:34] sidecar-57fd evict key hotkey-42 (bucket=hot)
[05:11:34] sidecar-57fd mem pressure: 92% used
[05:12:01] inference-runner WARN model-run slow: tail-latency 1800ms
[05:12:10] sidecar-57fd throttle begin
```
Priya: also noticing a short burst of large batch requests from one client IP range (10.34.x.x). Could be replay.
Sam: if it's KV thrash + sidecar CPU, immediate mitigations: 1) scale sidecar replicas 2) enable degraded model variant (quantized) fallback 3) route heavy traffic to dedicated pool. I can do 1 and 2.
Jordan: do it. I'll try to get quick heatmap and confirm customer impact before routing.
Jordan: customers: streaming sessions report increased latency/timeouts, some requests falling back to retries. Estimated impacted queries ~3-4% of overall QPS but concentrated in eu-west.
Sam: scaling sidecars now — running platform command:
```
# scale sidecar deployment in eu-west
kubectl -n inference scale deploy/sidecar-eu-west --replicas=24
```
Sam: enabling model fallback (small-quant) via feature flag (non-disruptive):
```
platformctl set feature inference-runtime.model_fallback=on --scope=eu-west
```
Tess: PagerDuty: Escalation triggered at +04m -> paging @Sam per policy (escalation).
Sam: done scaling and flip. Sidecar CPU drooped from 92% -> 68% in last 90s, p95 improved to ~420ms, p99 still ~1.1s (down from 2.9s). Looks like fallback helped tail but not fully recovered; eviction rate lowered though.
Priya: confirming KV hit rate down ~30% and eviction count stabilized. Still seeing a trailing tail from earlier bursts (KV warmup).
Jordan: good. I'm going to throttle source IP range at the edge to reduce noise and buy us time to warm caches.
Jordan: applying rate-limit rule (edge):
```
edgectl ratelimit add --src-range 10.34.0.0/16 --reqs-per-min 300 --scope eu-west
```
incident-bot: NOTE ADDED — action: edge rate-limit applied to 10.34.0.0/16 by Jordan (05:21 UTC).
Priya: after rate-limit, p99 dropped to ~650ms over the next 2m. Streaming error rate down to baseline.
Tess: please document customer impact for postmortem: which tenants hit timeouts, any paid-customers affected? Jordan, Priya can you capture list?
Jordan: grabbing logs for impacted tenants now — looks like 4 internal customers and 2 paying customers in eu-west saw >1s latencies and some 504s during the 05:11-05:20 window. I'll upload to the incident doc.
Sam: starting a partial traffic shift to dedicated pool to avoid repeated cold-cache thrash: routing 15% of traffic to dedicated-fallback-eu for 10m as canary.
Sam: command: `platformctl route split --service inference-runtime --region eu-west --alloc "primary=85,dedicated=15"`
Priya: can we warm the KV on dedicated-fallback-eu? I'll run a synthetic prompt spool to prime caches.
Priya: running warmup script now: `python tools/warm_kv.py --region eu-west --pool dedicated-fallback-eu --keys 5000`
Jordan: FYI ops note for handoff: primary mitigations executed: sidecar scale + fallback model enabled + edge rate-limit + 15% canary to dedicated pool + KV warmup. Visible impact: p95 back to target, p99 trending down to ~500-700ms.
PagerDuty: Incident INC-4321 acknowledged by Jordan, escalated to Sam, updates being posted to this thread.
Tess: do we need to open a rollback or code fix? Or is this operational (no code change)?
Priya: looks operational — noisy client + bad cache eviction. Recommend follow-ups: 1) client contact/email (solutions) 2) add defensive rate-limiter for unusually large batch sizes 3) investigate sidecar memory config (eviction thresholds).
Jordan: I'm going to hand off to Riley for the overnight watch and postmortem doc. I'll be offline in ~25m. Riley, please pick this up and verify the canary remains stable.
Riley: taking over. I'll keep an eye for 2h and confirm rollback of temporary rules once stable. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Note: manual suppression of PagerDuty repeat alerts set for 30m to avoid alert fatigue (actor=Jordan).
Tess: thanks all — initial severity remains P1 until p99 < 500ms for 15m. Current p99 ~520ms and trending down.
Riley: logging runbook checklist items into incident doc now, attaching charts and impacted tenant list.
Jordan: uploaded logs and tenant list to https://internal.incidents/INC-4321/docs (see attachment).
Sam: follow-up action items added: increase sidecar replica autoscaling responsiveness, add guardrail for large batch submissions, review default cache eviction policy.
Tess: postmortem owner: Riley. ETA for draft: EOD tomorrow.
Riley: acknowledged. I'll also coordinate customer comms with solutions team in the AM.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — resolved? Not yet. Monitoring continued; next auto-check in 10m.
Jordan: thanks everyone. Leaving handoff notes: all temporary mitigations are safe to keep for 30m while we observe.
Riley: I'll close the circle or escalate if p99 creeps back up.
Priya: small note — saved heap profiles and heapdump from sidecar-57fd at 05:13 UTC to /var/tmp/INC-4321/ for postmortem.
Sam: :thumbsup: good capture.
__meta_notes: Generated synthetic Slack thread for eng-oncall about p99 latency paging; single continuous string of messages, messages prefixed with sender names; includes bot and PagerDuty notices, commands, logs, mitigations, and handoff. Timestamps are synthetic but ordered.
